name: library.categories
description: Count the books under each category tag, most-used first, plus the books carrying no tag. Read this before passing `categories` to library.find_books: it is where this library's tag vocabulary can be seen, and a library nobody has tagged reports every book as uncategorised.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: library.find_books
description: Search the book registry by title substring (fuzzy), contributor name (exact), file format, or category tags. The `categories` filter matches books carrying at least one of the listed tags; library.categories lists the tags this library carries. `awaiting_text` lists the scan sources still without text.

awaiting_text.description:
When true, match only scan sources the library holds no text
for: a `needs_ocr` book with no book derived from it that was
ingested. Each row then carries an `awaiting_text` object with
the path of the scan, its SHA-256, its page count, and why its
text layer was rejected. `statuses: ["needs_ocr"]` alone also
lists the scans whose text is already in the library.

categories.description:
Match books carrying at least one of these category tags. An
empty list, like an absent one, imposes no category filter. The
tags a library carries are listed by `library.categories`; a tag
not listed there matches nothing.

contributor_name.description: Exact-equality match against a contributor name.

contributor_role.description:
Restrict the contributor filter to one role (`author` /
`translator` / `editor` / `other`). Only takes effect with
`contributor_name`.

format.description:
Exact-equality match against the file format (`epub`, `pdf`,
`rule-text`, ...).

language.description:
Match books whose reported language is one of these, compared
as text against the value the row carries (`de`, `en`, ...).
The pipeline does not normalise the tag, so match what
`show_book` reports.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

limit.description: Maximum number of books in this page.

offset.description: Number of leading rows to skip.

statuses.description:
Match books whose lifecycle status is one of these, named as
they are reported in a row's `status`: `pending`, `extracted`,
`dedup_hold`, `embedded`, `aborted`, `needs_ocr`. Only an
`embedded` book has vectors, so only an `embedded` book can be
recalled by the search tools. An unrecognised name is refused
rather than dropped.

title_substring.description:
Substring match against the book title as reported, i.e. with
the curator's corrections applied.

name: library.find_papers
description: Search the paper registry by title substring (fuzzy), contributor name (exact), year (exact), venue substring (matched against container title), or DOI (exact). Mirrors library.find_books for the paper pipeline; rows carry source_filename like library.list_papers.

contributor_name.description: Exact-equality match against a contributor name.

contributor_role.description:
Restrict the contributor filter to one role (`author` /
`translator` / `editor` / `other`). Only takes effect with
`contributor_name`.

doi.description: Exact-equality match against the reported DOI.

language.description:
Match papers whose reported language is one of these, compared
as text against the value the row carries (`de`, `en`, ...).
The pipeline does not normalise the tag, so match what
`show_paper` reports.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

limit.description: Maximum number of papers in this page.

offset.description: Number of leading rows to skip.

statuses.description:
Match papers whose lifecycle status is one of these, named as
they are reported in a row's `status`: `pending`, `extracted`,
`embedded`. Only an `embedded` paper has vectors, so only an
`embedded` paper can be recalled by the search tools. The book
pipeline's three further states are not reachable here and are
refused, as is an unrecognised name.

title_substring.description:
Substring match against the paper title as reported, i.e. with
the curator's corrections applied. The three bibliographic
filters below read the same layer.

venue_substring.description:
Substring match against the reported container title (journal,
proceedings, ...).

year.description: Exact-equality match against the reported year.

name: library.info

library.description:

Each summary carries source_filename, the basename of the file the book was ingested from, which identifies a book whose title is missing or is an export-tool placeholder.

confidence_in.description:
Match the audit's row-level confidence against this set:
`low`, `medium`, `high`. An unrecognised name is refused rather
than dropped.

library.description:

Substring match against the title as extraction and enrichment
wrote it, before any correction — the layer a review pass asks
about. To search the titles rows report, use
`library.find_books`.

name: library.metadata.ack
description: Acknowledge a metadata gap on one book: the audit verdict is unchanged; the review row is flipped to `acknowledged` with the given reason. The book stays on the review queue until approved or rejected.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

reason.description: Why the gap is being acknowledged; recorded on the audit row.

name: library.metadata.approve
description: Approve the metadata record on one book: assert that the effective metadata matches the source. Flips the review row to `approved`. The audit verdict is unchanged.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

reason.description: Optional reason recorded on the audit row.

name: library.metadata.clear
description: Remove an override on one bibliographic field of one book, reverting to the extracted value. An editable field with no override still appends an audit row recording the attempt; an unknown field name is rejected unless a stale override row with that key exists. The required `reason` lands on the audit row.

field.description:
The field whose override should be removed. A name outside the
editable set is accepted only when an override row with that key
exists (cleanup of stale rows); otherwise it is rejected.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

reason.description:
Why the override is being removed. Recorded on the audit row;
required so an LLM edit always carries its justification.

name: library.metadata.contributor_add
description: Attribute a contributor (role: author / translator / editor / other) to one book. The row is written with origin `user`, survives re-ingest, and is immediately searchable via `library.find_books` `contributor_name`. Appends one audit row tagged `actor_kind=llm` carrying the required `reason`. Returns the new row's `contributor_id`.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

name.description: The contributor's name, exactly as it should be searchable.

reason.description:
Why this attribution is correct (e.g. the source consulted).
Recorded on the audit row; required so an LLM edit always
carries its justification.

name: library.metadata.contributor_remove
description: Remove one contributor row from one book by the `contributor_id` listed in `library.show_book`, whatever its origin — the path for stripping a wrong extracted attribution (e.g. an ebook packager credited as the author). Appends one audit row tagged `actor_kind=llm` carrying the required `reason`. A forced re-ingest re-seeds extracted rows, so such a removal may need repeating after one.

contributor_id.description:
Surrogate id of the contributor row, as listed by
`library.show_book`.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

reason.description:
Why the attribution is wrong. Recorded on the audit row;
required so an LLM edit always carries its justification.

name: library.metadata.reaudit
description: Re-run the metadata plausibility audit for one book from its cached extraction, refreshing the stored verdict and confidence so they reflect the current effective metadata (overrides included). Use after correcting fields so the stored `needs_work` / `low` can catch up. Grades under the library's audit profile and audit data overlays; the review status is untouched. Returns the previous and new verdict / confidence pair.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

name: library.metadata.reject
description: Reject one book: flip the review row to `rejected`. Pipeline rows stay in place so downstream consumers can filter on `rejected`. Records the reason on the audit row.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

reason.description: Why the book is being rejected; recorded on the audit row.

name: library.metadata.set
description: Set an override on one editable bibliographic field of one book. An unknown field name is rejected with the editable list in the error. The extracted value is preserved; the override wins on read. Appends one audit row tagged `actor_kind=llm` carrying the required `reason`. Pass `confirmed: true` only after verifying the value against the source itself; the audit then grades the field strong.

confirmed.description:
Set true only after checking the value against the source
itself (e.g. the copyright page via `library.read_span`), not
against an external catalog alone. The audit grades a confirmed
override strong unless a validation check fails. Defaults to
false.

field.description:
The field to set. Must be a curator-editable bibliographic
field; an unknown name is rejected and the error carries the
full editable list.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

reason.description:
Why this value is correct (e.g. the source consulted). Recorded
on the audit row; required so an LLM edit always carries its
justification.

name: library.metadata.void
description: Suppress one field's extracted value without supplying a replacement: the field reads as absent until a correct value is set. For extracted values known to be wrong when no right value is at hand. `library.metadata.clear` removes the suppression. Appends one audit row tagged `actor_kind=llm` carrying the required `reason`.

field.description:
The field whose extracted value should be suppressed. Must be a
curator-editable bibliographic field.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Write tools require an
explicit selector so a misrouted call never silently lands on
the wrong library's catalog.

reason.description:
Why the extracted value is wrong. Recorded on the audit row;
required so an LLM edit always carries its justification.

name: library.read_context
description: Read the passages surrounding one anchor passage, in document order: N leaves before and N after, paragraph-precise. Pass the node_id from a search citation's start_node_id or from a passage of a previous read. Returns null when no such node exists; rejects organizing nodes (read those with library.read_span).

after.description:
Number of leaves to include after the anchor. Defaults to 3;
clamped server-side.

before.description:
Number of leaves to include before the anchor. Defaults to 3;
clamped server-side.

kind.description:
Which pipeline the anchor node belongs to (`book` for ingest,
`paper` for glean). Defaults to `book` via
[`ItemKind::default`] so existing callers stay green; pass
`paper` to read context from the papers corpus.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused. Unrelated to `kind`.

node_id.description:
Corpus node id of the anchor leaf — take it from a search
citation's `start_node_id` or from a passage of a previous
read.

name: library.read_span
description: Read the full text under one TOC node (chapter, section, ...) in document order, paginated by a character budget. Pass the node_id from library.show_toc; to continue, pass the returned next_offset back as start_after until next_offset is null. Returns null when no such node exists; rejects leaf nodes (read around those with library.read_context).

kind.description:
Which pipeline the target node belongs to (`book` for ingest,
`paper` for glean). Defaults to `book` via
[`ItemKind::default`] so existing callers stay green; pass
`paper` to read from the papers corpus.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused. Unrelated to `kind`.

node_id.description:
Corpus node id of the organizing node (chapter, section, ...)
to read — take it from `library.show_toc`.

start_after.description:
Resume cursor: the `next_offset` of the previous page. Omit to
read from the span's start.

name: library.search
description: Search the library for passages relevant to a natural-language query. Returns cited passages, nearest first, each with a breadcrumb trail and source location. `kind` selects which side: `"book"` (the default; existing behaviour), `"paper"` (only the paper-side store), or `"all"` (both stores, merged by ascending distance). To suppress books you have already read or judged irrelevant, pass their intake ids in `exclude_book_intake_ids` (or `exclude_paper_intake_ids` for papers); the ids must match the `kind` being searched.

bypass_index.description:
Force a brute-force scan, ignoring any ANN index. Useful for
ground-truth checks.

exclude_book_intake_ids.description:
Catalog intake ids of books whose passages must not be returned.
Omit or pass an empty list to filter nothing. Applies to `kind`
`"book"` and `"all"`; passing it with `kind="paper"` is an
error, since the two id name spaces are unrelated. Ids that name
no book simply exclude nothing. `library.search_in_book` takes
no exclusions — recall is already confined to one book there.

exclude_paper_intake_ids.description:
Catalog intake ids of papers whose passages must not be
returned. The paper-side mirror of `exclude_book_intake_ids`:
applies to `kind` `"paper"` and `"all"`, and passing it with
`kind="book"` is an error.

kind.description:
Which side of the library to search: `"book"` (the default —
existing behaviour), `"paper"` (only the paper-side store),
or `"all"` (both stores, merged by ascending distance).

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

nprobes.description:
Override the IVF probe count for this query only. Higher values
trade latency for recall; the persisted meta default applies when
omitted.

query.description: The natural-language query to search the library for.

refine_factor.description:
Override the IVF-PQ refinement multiplier for this query only.
The persisted meta default applies when omitted.

top_k.description:
Maximum number of passages to return. Defaults to the server's
configured top-k when omitted.

name: library.search_in_book
description: Search a single book for passages relevant to a query. Pass the book's intake_id (from library.list_books / library.show_book). Returns cited passages, nearest first.

bypass_index.description: Force a brute-force scan, ignoring any ANN index.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book to confine recall to.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

nprobes.description: Override the IVF probe count for this query only.

refine_factor.description: Override the IVF-PQ refinement multiplier for this query only.

top_k.description: Maximum number of passages to return.

name: library.search_in_paper
description: Search a single paper for passages relevant to a query. Pass the paper's intake_id (from library.list_papers / library.show_paper). Returns cited passages, nearest first.

bypass_index.description: Force a brute-force scan, ignoring any ANN index.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the paper to confine recall to.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon

nprobes.description: Override the IVF probe count for this query only.

refine_factor.description: Override the IVF-PQ refinement multiplier for this query only.

top_k.description: Maximum number of passages to return.

name: library.show_audit_trail
description: Return the metadata-edit audit trail for one book, oldest first. Returns null when no such book is registered.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:

name: library.show_book
description: Fetch the full bibliographic record for one book by intake id. Returns effective biblio attributes, the active overrides (which fields are curated rather than extracted, by whom and when; `value: null` marks a suppressed extracted value), the contributor list, the source-side record of the ingested file (source_path / source_filename / source_sha256 / intake_at / page_count / byte_size; source_path is recorded verbatim at intake, so it may be relative or no longer exist on disk), and toc_stats (entry_count / max_depth of the ingested TOC; null when nothing is ingested) — check toc_stats before library.show_toc to pick a pagination or projection strategy. Returns null when no such book is registered.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: library.show_metadata_audit
description: Return the metadata-status record for one book: the bibliographic detail plus the persisted audit verdict, confidence, and current review status. Returns null when no such book is registered.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:

route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else

name: library.show_metadata_report
description: Recompute the metadata plausibility audit for one book from its cached extraction and return the full per-field report: origin (extracted / override / override_confirmed / voided), grade, flags, and hint per field, plus TOC shape flags and copyright-page block candidates, next to the stored verdict / confidence rollup for comparison. Use it to see why a book is `needs_work` / `low` before editing. Grades under the library's audit profile and audit data overlays, as library.metadata.reaudit does; nothing is written back — library.metadata.reaudit is the write path that refreshes the stored rollup. Returns null when no such book is registered.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

Mirrors library.show_book for the paper pipeline, toc_stats included; the abstract text is in the detail response, not in list summaries. Also returns the source-side record of the ingested file (source_path / source_filename / source_sha256 / intake_at / page_count / byte_size; source_path is recorded verbatim at intake, so it may be relative or no longer exist on disk — papers.fetch_source locates the archived copy instead). Returns null when no such paper is registered.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the paper.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else

name: library.show_paper_audit_trail
description: Return the metadata-edit audit trail for one paper, oldest first: who changed which field, what it said before, and why. Returns null when no such paper is registered and no edits were ever recorded against the id.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the paper.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: library.show_paper_metadata_report
description: Recompute the metadata plausibility audit for one paper from its cached extraction and return the full per-field report: origin (extracted / override / override_confirmed / voided), grade, flags, and hint per field, plus the cross-field flags and the CSL type the required-field matrix was selected by. Each response also carries the judgement stored on the paper's audit row; the two disagreeing means the paper was edited after that judgement was made. Grades under the library's paper audit profile and audit data overlays, or under the built-in profile `audit_profile` names; nothing is written back. No tool writes paper metadata: the operator's `bookrack papers metadata reaudit <intake_id>` brings the stored row back in line. Returns null when no such paper is registered.

audit_profile.description:
Paper-side audit profile to grade under: `default`,
`trust_source`, or `strict`. Omit to grade under the library's
own profile overlay. Another name is refused.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the paper.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: library.show_paper_toc
description: Return the table of contents of one paper. Papers carry one Work root plus one prose leaf, so the TOC is effectively empty for a well-formed paper. The shape, the offset / limit / next_offset pagination contract, and the titles_only / max_depth / title_substring parameters mirror library.show_toc for the book pipeline.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book or paper.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

limit.description:
Maximum TOC entries in this page. Defaults to and is clamped
by the server-side cap (2000); around 200 keeps responses
small.

max_depth.description:
Keep only entries at depth <= max_depth. The book root is
depth 0, so 1 keeps the root plus its top-level divisions.

offset.description:
Number of leading TOC entries to skip. Pass a previous
response's `next_offset` here to read the following page.

title_substring.description:
Keep only entries whose title contains this substring,
ignoring ASCII case. The cheap way to locate one chapter or
section by name.

titles_only.description:
Return slim entries carrying only node_id, title, and depth —
the cheap way to scan a book's structure. The node_id feeds
library.read_span.

name: library.show_pipeline_trail
description: Return the book-level pipeline audit trail for one book, oldest first. Each row records a pipeline sub-step (stage, outcome, duration, run id). Returns null when no such book is registered.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: library.show_toc
description: Return the table of contents of one book: a depth-first list of organizing nodes (chapters, sections, ...) with their titles, depths, and document-order spans, paginated. To continue, pass the returned next_offset back as offset until next_offset is null; total counts every matching entry. A limit of about 200 keeps responses small. To scan structure, prefer titles_only (each entry keeps node_id / title / depth; node_id is what library.read_span takes) and max_depth (1 = root plus top-level divisions). To locate one chapter or section by name, filter with title_substring instead of paging the whole TOC. Returns null when no such book is ingested.

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the book or paper.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

limit.description:
Maximum TOC entries in this page. Defaults to and is clamped
by the server-side cap (2000); around 200 keeps responses
small.

max_depth.description:
Keep only entries at depth <= max_depth. The book root is
depth 0, so 1 keeps the root plus its top-level divisions.

offset.description:
Number of leading TOC entries to skip. Pass a previous
response's `next_offset` here to read the following page.

title_substring.description:
Keep only entries whose title contains this substring,
ignoring ASCII case. The cheap way to locate one chapter or
section by name.

titles_only.description:
Return slim entries carrying only node_id, title, and depth —
the cheap way to scan a book's structure. The node_id feeds
library.read_span.

name: library.stats
description: Return aggregate counts over the library: intakes by status and format, book states by pipeline stage, and retrieval issues by triage status.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: library.vectors_status
description: Snapshot the vector store: chunk-table row count, every ANN index LanceDB enumerates with its per-shard statistics, the persisted ANN config, and any drift between the on-disk meta and the indices LanceDB actually carries.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: papers.fetch_source
description: Return the absolute path, byte size, and SHA-256 of one paper's archived source PDF. The client opens the path with its own file-system primitives — the bytes do not flow through the control plane. Returns null when the intake id is unknown; raises an error when the intake exists but its source PDF was not archived (e.g. glean ran with `keep_source_pdf = false`).

intake_id.description: Catalog intake id of the paper.

library.description:
Library short name from the registry. Omit to let the daemon
route the call: the registry default when it is mounted, else
the only mounted library; otherwise the call is refused.

name: reference.lookup
description: Look up a reference-book entry by its normalized key. `book` is either a specific book slug or `*` to query every registered book and rank cross-book hits by authority_rank. `fields` optionally restricts which payload keys appear on each hit; `min_severity` (ok | info | warn | error) drops hits whose quality_flags carry no concern at or above that severity. Single-hit redirect entries auto-follow one hop.

book.description:
Book slug to scope the lookup to. Pass `"*"` to query every
registered book and rank cross-book hits by `authority_rank`.

entry_key.description:
The lookup key; resolves directly against
`reference_entries.entry_key`.

exclude_books.description:
Book slugs whose entries must not be returned. Only meaningful
with `book = "*"`, where the lookup spans every registered
book; passing it alongside a single-book scope is an error
rather than a no-op. An excluded book is also skipped as a
redirect target, so it cannot re-enter the result that way.

fields.description:
Optional payload-key whitelist. When `Some`, payload keys
outside the list are stripped from each hit.

min_severity.description:
Optional quality_flag-severity floor. When set, hits whose
flags do not include at least one flag at or above this
severity drop out. Recognised values: `ok`, `info`, `warn`,
`error`.

name: reference.overlay_set
description: Layer a user edit on top of one reference entry. Every key in `overlay` must be in property_catalog.toml. `reason` is a free-text edit summary recorded on the overlay row. The `edited_at` stamp is set to the daemon's current UTC time.

overlay.description:
JSON object whose keys must be present in the property
catalog (`crates/distill/data/property_catalog.toml`).

reason.description: Free-text edit summary recorded on the overlay row.

name: session.info
description: Daemon runtime summary: bookrack version, uptime, the libraries this session has mounted (each with its data root and whether it is the default), the registered libraries it did not mount (each with its data root and the reason), the default library, MCP listener address, and Ollama endpoint.

name: session.logs_tail
description: Return the most recent N log events from the daemon's in-memory ring buffer (oldest first within the returned slice). N defaults to 100 and is capped server-side at 1024.

n.description:
Maximum number of log events to return, from the most recent.
Capped server-side at [`bookrack_obs::stream::TAIL_REQUEST_MAX`];
defaults to [`bookrack_obs::stream::TAIL_REQUEST_DEFAULT`] when
omitted.

name: session.queue_status
description: Snapshot of the ingest queue: counts by lifecycle state across the whole queue, plus the most recently enqueued jobs (newest first, capped at 10). `state` lists only jobs in that state, so `{"state": "failed"}` finds failures however early they were enqueued; a failed job carries its `error` and, when the daemon classified the failure, a `problem` with summary, detail, hint and retryable. Returns an empty snapshot when run against a daemon that does not host a queue worker.

state.description:
List only jobs in this lifecycle state in `recent`, under the
same cap and order. The names are the ones a row reports in its
`state`: `pending`, `running`, `done`, `skipped_duplicate`,
`needs_ocr`, `failed`, `cancelled`. The counts cover the whole
queue either way. An unrecognised name is refused rather than
dropped.

name: session.shutdown
description: Ask the daemon to perform a graceful shutdown. Returns immediately after firing the shutdown signal; the listener and queue worker then wind down asynchronously.
